KandirosHarshawSavje2026 Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5 define the same q=2 labeled graph minimax game and prove its equality to unrestricted ANI minimax risk after restriction to maximal independent sets.

KandirosHarshawSavje2026 develops design-based mixture lower bounds; AronowLopatto2026 uses a vertex-prior Bayes-risk argument in a different unbiased sampling problem. Neither states this conflict-constrained certificate program.
HarshawMiddletonSavje2022 studies symmetry-compatible conservative quadratic variance bounds, but not posterior-risk lower certificates for the unrestricted conflict-graph game.

novelty_flags.label: thm:finite-prior-weak-duality; flagship framing
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed certificate innovation is positioned against only KandirosHarshawSavje2026 and AronowLopatto2026, without a located comparison to the finite-population minimax and least-favourable-prior literature (for example Gabler 2012 and Rinott 2009); this does not yet establish that the ordinary Bayes-risk lower-bound move is a flagship causal advance.

soundness_flags.label: thm:finite-prior-weak-duality
soundness_flags.one_line: The asserted weak duality is only the posterior-mean Bayes action followed by Bayes risk no larger than worst-case risk, so it is a clean one-to-two-step reduction and caps this flagship-targeted kernel at field tier unless strengthened by a non-routine duality or approximation theorem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 7–8, definition of M(G,τ,q); pp. 36–41, Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5, especially Proposition A.6 and Lemmas A.8–A.10
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper imposes separate q-moment restrictions for the two contrast exposures, defines graph minimax problems over independent and maximal independent sets, proves an injective maximal-independent-set realization map, and proves equality of the unrestricted ANI minimax risk and the maximal-independent-set minimax problem.

The paper constructs Conflict Graph Design and analyzes modified Horvitz--Thompson estimation with finite-sample upper-risk/variance guarantees under ANI; it is not an unrestricted minimax lower-certificate result.

Theorems 1–3 concern lower bounds and optimal designs among unbiased estimators for bounded rectangular finite-population sampling models, using a vertex-prior argument; the setting is not conflict-constrained ANI minimax estimation over all measurable estimators.

The paper defines and optimizes conservative, design-compatible upper bounds on the variance of a point estimator through quadratic forms; it does not provide a lower certificate for unrestricted minimax MSE.

The article presents CauseIS as an independent-set-based framework for direct-effect experiments and reports empirical estimation-error improvements; it does not give a minimax or posterior-risk certificate.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the already-published primal-identity theorem with a genuinely stronger result: prove finite-prior strong duality or a quantitative constant-factor certificate theorem on a named nontrivial graph family, with its approximation factor derived from graph structure.

Turn the block-clique counting result into an exact or constant-factor minimax theorem for the full G_{b,s} family by giving an optimal invariant design, an explicit prior, and matching values rather than only orbit counts.

Add located comparisons to finite-population minimax and least-favourable-prior work, then state precisely which obstruction—conflict-constrained observations, unrestricted estimators, or simultaneous design choice—prevents those results from subsuming the proposed certificate.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision on this angle: make a non-routine duality or algorithmic approximation theorem, rather than the source-duplicated primal identity and routine weak-duality certificate, the flagship solve target.
